Q: How do I evaluate a string expression in SQL Server? A:

If you need to have the value in a variable, not only select it, one possibility is to use a temporary table to insert the value into.

declare @expr nvarchar(max) = '100+200'; -- this could be a parameter, or similar, as well
declare @vals(val int); -- here you must know the result type
declare @val int; -- the same here
insert into @vals(val) exec (@expr); -- cannot be used inside a function, neither inside a procedure to return result to be inserted in a table, because multilevel insert with exec does not work
select @val = val from @vals; -- here you have the result as variable value

For arithmetic expression evaluation, please see https://users.drew.edu/skass/sql/infix.sql.txt

Q: Storing important and not-important data in Redis? A:

Redis does not support priority per key.
Use no TTL for important data, TTL for disposable cache data, and set a volatile-* eviction policy.
If important data also needs TTL and must not be evicted early, use a separate Redis instance for it.

Q: What is an Interface in Java? A:

unless you want to count default method, there is no inheritance of functionality when using interfaces, and default methods should not be used often.

when you implement an interface, you don't really override a method, rather than implement it.

For instance:

interface ICar {
void accelerate();
}

or

class Vehicle {
double speed = 0.0;

void accelerate() {
this.speed += 2.0;
}
}

Let's say you have a sportscar and a family car. obviously, the 'accelerate' won't be the same for both, but if you use the super class, you can't be sure it doesn't use the same implementation.

With an interface, you literally force a class to provide it's own implementation (unless of course it also extends a class that provides an implementation).

If you use a class to inherit, you force specific behavior and limitations on your code, unless of course you go and completely override all methods that would also appear in the interface, but, if you do that: what is the use of having a super class at all?
